title: Cheeseburger on Wheat Bun with Large Patty

content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a wheat bun, a large beef patty (about 150 g) and melted cheese. The patty is grilled or pan‑fried, and the bun is often lightly toasted. Common additions include lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles and various sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the United States in the 1920s.
A wheat bun gives a softer texture compared with the traditional sesame‑seed bun.
A 150 g patty is considered a “super‑size” portion and is common in fast‑food chains.
Cheese melts at around 70 °C, creating the characteristic stretchy layer.
Cheeseburgers are typically served with french fries and a soft drink.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: A cheeseburger provides a quick source of calories, useful for high‑energy needs.

items.title: High calories and fat
items.content: The large patty and cheese make the cheeseburger calorie‑dense and high in saturated fat; moderation is advised.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt in the bun, sauces, and cheese can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Potential meat pathogens
items.content: Undercooked patty may harbor bacteria such as E. coli or salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding the bottom of the bun. Add sauces, vegetables, or extra toppings to taste. The patty can be swapped for turkey or a plant‑based alternative if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best consumed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or skillet, toasting the bun separately to keep it from becoming soggy.
